definitions.explanation: A situation or action that must be accepted because there is no alternative.

examples.japanese: {事情|じじょう}があってやむを{得|え}ず{欠席|けっせき}した。
examples.english: Due to circumstances, I had no choice but to be absent.

examples.japanese: やむを{得|え}ない{事情|じじょう}がある{場合|ばあい}は{連絡|れんらく}してください。
examples.english: Please contact us if there are unavoidable circumstances.

examples.japanese: この{状況|じょうきょう}では{延期|えんき}もやむを{得|え}ない。
examples.english: Under these circumstances, postponement is unavoidable.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
やむ (to cease, stop) + を (object particle) + {得|え}ない (cannot obtain) → cannot make it stop = unavoidable

FORMS:
・やむを{得|え}ない{事情|じじょう} - unavoidable circumstances
・やむを{得|え}ず (adverb) - unavoidably, having no choice
・やむを{得|え}ない{場合|ばあい} - when unavoidable

GRAMMAR:
This is a set expression. やむ is the classical verb meaning "to cease" and を{得|え}ない is the negative potential form of {得|え}る (to obtain).

USAGE:
Common in formal and business contexts as an explanation or justification. Often used in written notices and announcements.

SYNONYMS:
・{仕方|しかた}がない - can't be helped (more casual)
・{致|いた}し{方|かた}ない - unavoidable (formal)
